photos.c: Above: Not only did Marlon Dickson pick up an All-England medal while running for London in the 4x100m, he also set new Club Record figures for our U15 100m by running 11.70.

Front page: ... And to think that we used to know him as "little Marlon". Shown here at the McDonald's YA League at Peterborough matching strides out of the blocks with Blackheath's Mark Findlay, Marlon Dickson had a great 1994 season. At 15 years of age he set personal bests of 11.36 and 23.1 and ran anchor leg for our U17M record breaking 4x100 quartette. He looks set to make a name for himself in 1995 when he remains in the same age-group and has already clocked 7.1 for an indoor 60m at the 'Palace'. Each season so far he has chopped 4/10ths off his 100m best. Another improvement like that would give him 10.96. Phil Goedluck's U17M record? - 10.96!

Below: The season comes to a close with Pat's Brats celebrating their second successive Rosenheim Final victory. Left to right - Jamie Webb, ? (obscured), Marlon Dickson, Matt George, Phil Goedluck, Mike Small, Pat Mead, Marcello Bizio (obscured), Roger Alsop, Jim Braben, Pete Mercer, Dave Pamah, Dalton Powell, Richard David.
Above: Unbeaten in any under-17 McDonald's sprint in 1995, Marlon Dickson

Half of the awesome foursome. Our Junior Men cracked the 4x100m, 4x200m and 4x400m Club Records in 1996 and these two had a hand in every one of those performances. Richard David, passing the baton, joined us at 15 years of age and last season, at 19, set pbs of 10.98, 22.1 and 48.7. Seventeen years-old Marlon Dickson has been with us since he was 12 and this year has run 10.65, 21.6 and a 49.2 relay leg.
The A.A.A. Under 20 Championships at Bedford sees Marlon Dickson (nearest the camera) and Richard David (far side) make a blistering two pronged Belgrave attack in the 100 metres.
